title: The Biggest Landslide Ever Recorded
description: In 1980 the north face of Mount St. Helens collapsed in the largest landslide in recorded history. Here is what set it off, how fast it moved, and what it left behind.
comment: Had you heard of Mount St. Helens before? What should we cover next?

scenes.narration: In 1980, a mountain in Washington lost its entire north face in seconds.
An earthquake shook loose the bulging side of Mount St. Helens.
It became the largest landslide in recorded history, racing downhill at up to 250 kilometres an hour.
With that weight suddenly gone, the volcano blew out sideways and flattened forests for miles.
The rubble filled the valley below, in places 180 metres deep.
Scientists still study that morning to learn how a mountain can fail.
